title: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
key_facts: OpenAI updated its ChatGPT extension for Google Chrome.
With the extension, ChatGPT can view open tabs when the user tags Chrome in the web or desktop app.
OpenAI's demo video shows ChatGPT comparing three open tabs of sofas.
The sidebar now offers the full ChatGPT with the whole conversation history in Chat or Work.
ChatGPT Work can control tabs: sending messages, filling out forms, downloading files, and organizing or grouping tabs.
The Verge compares it with Google's Gemini-powered auto browse.
The article notes the ChatGPT Atlas browser is gone.
quote_evidence: OpenAI says ChatGPT can now view your browser tabs when you tag Chrome in ChatGPT's web or desktop app.
It also enables ChatGPT Work to "control" your Chrome tabs for tasks like "sending messages, filling out forms, or downloading files"
why_it_matters_hint: Gives the assistant direct access to what a user is browsing and lets it act on pages.
notes: Short article (about 1,200 characters); a list of sample queries did not come through. No safeguards or availability details in the text.
